draft:
We are writing to inform you of a new investment in the Urbis Logistics Portfolio, a portfolio of 11 last-mile logistics properties located in major European urban areas. The transaction values the Portfolio at EUR 612 million, representing a going-in net initial yield of 5.4 percent and approximately EUR 1,820 per lettable square metre.

The Portfolio comprises 337,000 square metres of lettable area distributed across Greater London (89,000 sqm in three assets), Greater Paris (72,000 sqm in three assets), Greater Amsterdam (64,000 sqm in two assets), Greater Madrid (71,000 sqm in two assets), and Greater Milan (41,000 sqm in one asset). All eleven assets are within 15 kilometres of city centres and serve last-mile delivery operations for major e-commerce platforms, grocery delivery operators, and parcel logistics players.

Occupancy is 96 percent and the weighted average unexpired lease term is 6.8 years. Contracted annual rental income is EUR 33.1 million. Importantly, embedded rental reversion across the Portfolio is estimated at approximately 18 percent, concentrated in the London and Amsterdam assets where market rents have grown most rapidly over the past three years.

Urban last-mile is one of the most structurally supported segments of European commercial real estate. Demand growth — driven by continued e-commerce penetration and same-day/next-day delivery expectations — is running well ahead of supply, which is constrained by urban planning priorities and political resistance to logistics development in city centres.

Our value creation plan rests on capturing the embedded reversion as approximately 40 percent of leases roll during the hold period, executing a EUR 38 million value-add capex programme to modernise three older assets, and benefiting from continued rental growth and modest yield compression. Levered at 55 percent loan-to-value, the base case generates an equity gross IRR of 16.8 percent and an MOIC of 2.1x over a five-year hold.
